card.statement:
<<cite:BK3>>
The action of $H_d$ on $V^{\otimes d}$ factors through
$H_d^{[\la]}$ and this gives rise to commuting actions:

$$
\W \; \stackrel{\Phi_{d}}{\curvearrowright} \; V^{\otimes d} \;
\stackrel{\Psi_{d}}{\curvearrowleft} \; H_d^{[\la]}.
$$

The maps $\Phi_{d}$ and $\Psi_d$ satisfy the double centralizer
property, i.e.

\begin{align*}
\Phi_{d}(\W)=&\End_{H_d^{[\la]}}(V^{\otimes d}),\\
&\End_{\W}(V^{\otimes d})^{\operatorname{op}} =
\Psi_d(H_d^{[\la]}).
\end{align*}
card.label: Theorem 60

paper.title: Nilpotent orbits and finite $W$-algebras
paper.abstract: In recent years, the finite W-algebras associated to a semisimple Lie algebra and its nilpotent element have been studied intensively from different viewpoints. In this lecture series, we shall present some basic constructions, connections, and applications of finite W-algebras.
